newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon stocks mixed, investors liquidate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon stocks mixed, investors liquidate.

text.p: Singapore stocks were mixed at midday Tuesday with institutional investors continuing to trim their portfolios, dealers said.
The retreat in the Dow Jones on Monday and bearish tone in Malaysian stocks also cast a gloom over the local market.
"Institutions don't see the value there and are liquidating their exposure," one dealer with a local brokerage said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index was up 6.26 points at 2,044.15 during the lunchtime break.
Decliners outnumbered gainers by 212 to 65 on a modest volume of 67 million shares.
Dealers said retail investors were also cutting losses on Malaysian over-the-counter issues, but falls would be limited as outright values had already been sliding for sometime.
Among losers was Keppel Corp, which sank to 44-month lows at Singapore $8.60, spurred by an unexciting earnings outlook for 1997. The share later revived five cents to S$8.75.
Singapore Telecom also dropped precipitously, touching new lows at S$2.65. It was down six cents at $2.66 at noon.
Net gainers were SPH foreign and Creative Technology, both of which recaptured some of their lost lustre.
